title.narrative: World Bank URTF MDTF Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, Reform
World Bank URTF, MDTF Ukraina, hjälp återhämtning, återuppbyggn., reform

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the URTF is to assist the government of Ukraine to: 1) sustain its administrative and service delivery capacity and conduct relief efforts; and 2) plan and implement Ukraine's recovery, resilient reconstruction and reform agenda.
Through the formulated preference in the administrative agreement Sida will seek to especially contribute to: - Increased capacity to ensure emergency heat and electricity supply for people and institutions in Ukraine. - Enhanced, life sustaining domestic heating and hot water heating for domestic dwellings and key institutions in Ukraine. - Re-established functionality of electricity transmission and distribution within Ukraine. - Restored ability to trade electricity between Ukraine and Europe.

Det övergripande målet för Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Trust Fund (URTF) är att hjälpa Ukrainas regering att:
1) upprätthålla sin administrativa kapacitet att tillhandahålla tjänster och genomföra hjälpinsatser; och 2) planera och genomföra Ukrainas återhämtning, motståndskraftiga återuppbyggnad och reformagenda.
Sverige har gjort en mjuk öronmärkning (62% av det svenska bidraget) för finansiering av omedelbara energibehov genom fondens energiprojekt (RePower).
För mer information om fondens aktiviteter se www.worldbank.org/en/programs/urtf

The overall objective of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Trust Fund (URTF) is to assist the Government of Ukraine to:
1) maintain its administrative capacity to provide services and implement relief efforts; and 2) planning and implementing Ukraine's recovery, resilient reconstruction and reform agenda.
Sweden has indicated a preference (62 % of the Swedish contribution) to finance immediate energy needs through the fund's energy project RePower. For more information regarding the fund's activities please visit: www.worldbank.org/en/programs/urtf

description.narrative:
This summary is based on the URTF Annual report 2024 (Archive case 22/00163164), unless otherwise stated.
Since establishment in 2022, the URTF has mobilized more than USD 2.8 billion in donor support, committed and programmed USD 2,6 billion and disbursed USD 1,8 billion. The URTF as such is country grant platform but it has also helped unlock USD 7.3 billion in additional development financing and mobilize USD 3.2 billion in private sector capital. It is perhaps especially important to emphasize to the point on the leveraging of private capital. The agriculture project ARISE is the World Banks (globally) largest private sector leveraging project.
Pillar 1 Pillar 1 Government Capacity and Relief) URTF played a critical role in helping the Ukrainian government to continue to function under wartime conditions. URTF supported operations sustained core government capacity while enabling the continued delivery of essential services. The five original framework projects are key projects under this pillar and they include the Ukraine Agriculture Recovery Inclusive Support Emergency (ARISE) Project, Health Enhancement and Lifesaving (HEAL) Ukraine Project, Housing Repair for Peoples Empowerment (HOPE) Project, Repairing Essential Logistics Infrastructure and Network Connectivity (RELINC) Project, Restoration Project of Winterization and Energy Resources (REPOWER) and Public Expenditures for Administrative Capacity Endurance (PEACE) Project.
Below follows a summary of what has been achieved by these projects. When studying these results one should bear in mind that these have been achieved using all financing available (which includes loans, guarantees and parallel co financing, and commercial financing from various actors also beyond the World Bank).
HEAL The Objective of HEAL is to restore and improve access to essential health care, address new and urgent needs for health services, and provide financial protection in an emergency context. Component 1. Mental Health and Rehabilitation Services Results examples:
- More than 655,000 people have received mental health services. Sixty psychological relief spaces are being established and equipped in PHC settings to increase community level access to mental health services. - More than 772,000 people completed a course of physical rehabilitation Over 3,100 pieces of rehabilitation equipment have been delivered to 198 health care facilities across 22 oblasts. - Capital renovation or reconstruction works of rehabilitation departments were initiated in eight facilities across six oblasts. - More than 8,200 PHC professionals were trained in providing care for survivors of gender-based violence (GBV).
Component 2. Primary Health Care Results examples: - More than 11.7 million people have received expanded PHC examinations. - Nearly 7 million doses of essential childhood vaccines were provided to children. - More than 5.7 million people were provided with subsidized medicines under Ukraine's Affordable Medicines Program. - For power supply resilience and efficiency, 130 PHC facilities in 19 oblasts have completed the installation of solar photovoltaic power stations. Solar panels, inverters, and battery storage systems help to ensure uninterrupted provision of power to medical services. - To support health care access in remote communities, 250 vehicles for providing mobile PHC services have been delivered to clinics nationwide. The total comprises 75 electric and 175 all terrain diesel vehicles. - 21 oblasts, 261 PHC facilities were equipped with hematology analyzers and accessories.
Component 3. Hospital care -Completed facilities include the Novobykivka Rural Outpatient Clinic (construction works), and Koziatyn City Primary Healthcare Center, and Primary Healthcare Outpatient Clinic No. 4 in Vinnytsia (capital repairs).
ARISE A total of 87,205 agricultural producers accessed financing, including 69,883 farmers reached through loans and grants. Nearly half of these farmers are women, significantly exceeding the projects inclusion targets. The project support the agriculture sector in two main ways, by reducing the cost of borrowing for larger commercial farms and by providing grants to smaller farms - Over 13.4 million hectares of agricultural land maintained under production, surpassing the projects original target of 8 million hectares. - Private capital amounting to $3.2 billion mobilized through ARISE supported financing more than double the projects original target of $1.5 billion, demonstrating strong leverage and market preserving design.
HOPE The objective of HOPE is to support affected households to regain adequate housing through repair of damaged housing stock and support national government in priority climate resilient policy reforms. Component 1 Repair of Residential Units with Partial Damage. Funding for the governments compensation program to affected households for emergency repair of partially damaged residential units or single family houses: Results examples: Over 130,000 households received financial support to repair their homes, restoring access to adequate housing across affected oblasts.
Component 2, Design and Capital Repair of Partially Damaged Multifamily Apartment Buildings. Green, resilient capital repairs of partially damaged multifamily buildings in selected municipalities: Results examples: Five cities, Bucha, Izyum, Makariv, Mykolaiv, and Zaporizhzhia were selected for support through a transparent and competitive process. Within these cities, 60 clusters, collectively comprising over 200 multifamily buildings, were identified for capital repairs using an innovative, datadriven methodology designed to enhance transparency, accountability, and impact.
RELINC The objective of RELINC is to provide the means for mitigating the immediate impact that disrupted transport networks have on Ukraine's population and economy. Component 1. Lifeline Road Connections Results examples: - Installation of several modular bridges, reflecting tangible advances in restoring damaged road links. -Preparation of bidding documentation for four additional modular bridges, with tenders scheduled for launch in the first quarter of 2026. Component 2. Lifeline Rail Connections Results example: - Signing of a €172.8 million contract by Ukrainian Railways for procurement of 20 electric locomotives, with delivery expected in 2027.
REPOWER The objective of the project is restoration of essential energy services through procuring critical equipment and supporting protective facilities
Component 1. Emergency Equipment for Electricity Transmission Infrastructure Results examples: -Delivered 13 autotransformers, 14 phase-shifting transformers, and seven transformers to 22 substations across the country As at December 31, 2025, the World Bank had agreed to support 25 level two protective shelters for autotransformers. The World Bank is also considering financing for an additional six shelters. Component 2. Emergency Equipment for Heating Services Results examples: - Delivered 43 items of heating equipment to the city of Kharkiv, including block modular boiler houses, pre-insulated pipes, and cogeneration gas units, which enabled rapid restoration of heat supply networks. - Launched requests for quotation for 45 cogeneration gas units to be distributed among Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Kremenchuk, Mykolaiv, and Slavuta, and for four boilers for Kryvyi Rih.
PEACE (Public Expenditures for Administrative Capacity Endurance Project) The objective of PEACE, which essentially is a budget support operation, is to contribute to sustaining the governments administrative and service delivery capacity to exercise core functions at the national and regional levels.
At the end of 2024,17 payments for salaries of eligible government, school, higher education, health care, and first responder personnel pensions and social assistance had been reimbursed in line with project design, supporting service delivery. The World Bank estimates that more than 13 million people had benefited from the PEACE project to end 2024 including: 10 million pensioners 500,000 education employees More than 140,000 government employees 56,000 first responders More than 3 million social assistance beneficiaries and internally displaced persons.
PILLAR 2 The work under this pillar is focused on strengthening institutional capacity and enabling implementation of priority reforms central to Ukraine's medium term recovery and European integration agenda. The portfolio constitutes a mix of Payment for Results projects, targeted project preparation interventions, technical assistance, capacity building and analytical products.
LEARN Program for Results, the objective of the program is to improve teaching and learning conditions and strengthen management capacity of the education system.
Component 1. Improving Teaching and Learning Conditions. Results examples: Expansion of access to education for 779,000 students, including through improved learning conditions and core education services.
Component 2. Improving Management Capacity. Results examples: - Promoting more datadriven, equitable, and transparent management of education sector funding programs. - Capacity building and implementation support to reinforce reform delivery, including preparations for the Grade 9 NUS pilot (in 145 schools), and strengthened Ministry of Education and Science systems for planning, monitoring, and coordinating nationwide reform implementation. -Training of more than 240,000 teachers in NUS aligned methodologies covering Grades 7 and 8, and supporting the phased rollout of the competency based curriculum.
RISE (Resilient, Inclusive, and Sustainable Enterprise Program for Results)
The objective of RISE is to improve the enabling environment for a sustainable private sector led recovery in Ukraine.
Component 1. Improving Efficiency of State Support to SMEs Results examples: - Mobilization of an additional USD 200 million in private capital, with 20 percent directed to female led SMEs. - Adoption of an environmental and social governance policy by the Business Development Fund. - Integration of environmental and social governance systems by over 20 banks, covering 90 percent of lending under the Affordable Loans 579 Program. 2. Improving the Business Environment and Government to Business Digital Services Results examples: - Launch and scaling of Diia.Business 2.0, to achieve more than 500,000 unique visits and reach 90,000 SME accounts. - Provision of tailored advisory and consulting services to 3,000 SMEs. 3. Enabling SME Access to Export Markets Results examples: - Adoption of the new Export Credit Agency Strategy, expanding product offerings. Support to 10 export oriented SME projects, including war risk coverage under the new strategy.
SURGE Supporting Reconstruction through Smart Fiscal Governance (SURGE) Program for Results. The objective of the program is to establish the institutional foundations for implementation and financing of climate smart recovery and reconstruction.
Component 1. Strengthening Public Investment Management Results examples: - Establishment of a unified, rules based PIM system, including adoption of a PIM Action Plan, staffing of dedicated PIM units in the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Economy, Environment, and Agriculture, and approval of standardized project preparation, appraisal, and prioritization methodologies. - Operationalisation of the Strategic Investment Council as the gatekeeper for public investment decisions. - Approval of the Single Project Pipeline of Public Investment for 2026 (149 projects and programs published on the DREAM portal). -Adoption of Budget Code amendments introducing the Medium-Term Priority Public Investment Plan and a unified definition of public investment. - Increased transparency through publication by the Ministry of Finance of the list of projects included in the state budget prior to parliamentary approval.
Component 2. Strengthening Local Public Financial Management Results examples: Updated budget methodologies enabling hromadas to prepare medium-term budgets incorporating gender information have now been applied and made publicly available to more than 400 hromadas.
Component 3. Improving Fiscal Governance at the Local Level Results examples: Introduction of transparent, rules based allocation of additional grants to hromadas affected by war, with clear eligibility criteria stipulated. Allocations have been made to at least 100 hromadas under the new framework.
4. Improving Revenue Administration Integrity - Launch of a risk based approach to tax audits, including the adoption of implementing regulations, Cabinet authorization of a pilot of the new approach,and identification of high risk taxpayers for audit selection.
THRIVE Transforming Health care through Reform and Investments in Efficiency program for Results. The objective of this program for results is to increase the efficiency of public expenditure on health.
Component 1. Prioritization within the PMG Results examples: Strengthened transparency and accountability in PHC financing through standardized capitation and data verification, improving predictability of payments, and ensuring that public resources are allocated to eligible patients and providers.
Component 2. Optimization of the Hospital Network Results examples: Publication by the NHSU of selective contracting thresholds for deliveries, surgeries, and stroke with thrombolysis, strengthening service concentration in higher capacity facilities and supporting quality and efficiency objectives. Preliminary data indicate a shift in selected inpatient care toward facilities meeting defined performance thresholds.
SPIRIT (Social Protection for Inclusion, Resilience, Innovation, and Transformation Technical Assistance Program). The objective of SPIRIT is to help the government develop and sustain inclusive, efficient, responsive social systems that address the needs of the most vulnerable populations and promote civil society participation in Ukraine's recovery.
Results examples: - Informed reform of employment regulation, labor market flexibility, and employment services for raising quality and employment impact. - Strengthened capacity of the State Employment Service for integrated case management of vulnerable unemployed persons. - Delivered analytics on womens' employment, active labor market programs, State Employment Service business processes, and digital readiness, informing the revision of the Labor Code, Employment Strategy 2030, and State Employment Service Strategy.
PREPARE Ukraine (Preparation of Resilient Projects to Advance Recovery of Ukraine). The objective of the project is to support Ukraine in developing a pipeline of implementation ready priority projects for reconstruction and recovery needs, and to build government capacity in project preparation.
Results examples : The PREPARE Ukraine operation finances the Ukraine Government Project Preparation Facility (Ukraine PPF). The Ukraine PPF is linked to the governments Public Investment Management (PIM) system and supports the preparation of projects prioritized by the government in the Single Project Pipeline of Public Investment (SPP). During 2025 the Ukraine PPF in coordination with project owners launched tenders for preparation of the three pilot investments allocated from the SPP under the PIM process.
Empowering Civil Society and Journalists in Oversight and Promotion of Effective Anticorruption Environment Project This is a slightly unusual project in that it is not directed towards government institutions. The project is implemented by a Ukrainian NGO, Anti Corruption Action Centre (ANTAC). The activities appears to center around analyses, monitoring, and dissemination of information of procurement processes, the developments in the judiciary (including court cases). It is not clear exactly how effective these activities have been.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
